items.a: Yes. There is no paid plan, no account and no usage limit.

items.q: Does it send my data anywhere?
items.a: No. Everything is analyzed in your browser. Only your settings are saved, and only on your computer.

50 of them: analytics (GA4, Adobe, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Segment, PostHog, Matomo and more), ad pixels (Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Ads, X, Pinterest, Snapchat, Reddit, Criteo and more), session recording, CRM, tag managers, A/B testing tools and the dataLayer.

items.q: My tool is not on the list. Can Hitline still show it?
items.a: Yes. Add it in Settings as a custom platform: a name and a part of its URL. Requests that only look like tracking are also listed under "Other".

items.q: How does it detect server-side GTM?
items.a: It checks where GA4 requests go, the request path, the server_container_url setting and cookies set by the server.

items.q: How is it different from Tag Assistant?
items.a: Tag Assistant focuses on Google tags. Hitline shows 50 platforms side by side, reads your GTM tags and triggers, checks consent, attribution and data quality, and compares events with your tracking plan.

The popup works without it and updates itself while open. For the full event stream, open DevTools and the Hitline tab, then reload the page once. Chrome does not let extensions open DevTools, so the popup shows the shortcut and DevTools opens on the event you clicked.
